clue.text: Inject a worker after developing limp

indicators.note: after says the worker piece comes behind the reworked letters
developing means changing shape, so the letters of the word limp are rearranged

parts.note: a worker is an ant, the typical worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer gets an injection once a limp sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a worker' reads as a person but is the insect; 'developing' rearranges LIMP to IMPL, and 'after' puts ANT behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant something is to insert or inject it into the body or a material.

clue.text: An American soldier set up superior base

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means lifted upward, so the soldier's letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
noble means superior in rank or character

explanation.surface: A US serviceman erects a better military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns GI into IG in this down clue; 'base' is the adjective, meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and ignoble both mean dishonourable or low in character.

clue.text: Turning pride into downfall

indicators.note: turning means changing, so the letters of pride and into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pride turns into a fall, as the proverb warns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges the nine letters of PRIDE INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdition is utter ruin or damnation, a spiritual fall.

clue.text: Gather there's a very large number on dope

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A huge amount of drugs is being collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces, ASS below the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate.

clue.text: The increase in the rate is put off

parts.note: tempo is the rate or speed of music
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A hike in interest rates has been postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: A rise in the tempo reads TEMPO RISE; 'in' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or stall for time.

clue.text: Being in more robust form, such a breather is not necessary

parts.note: being in is simply the word in, as in being at home
hale means robust or healthy, so in more robust form is haler

explanation.surface: Someone who is fitter has no need of a puffer for their breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'such a breather is not necessary' is a joke on the wordplay: a person IN HALER form needs no puffer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is one who breathes in, and also the device used to help breathing.

clue.text: Not out just to furnish

parts.note: not out is in, as a cricket batter who is still at the crease
just means deserved, which is due

explanation.surface: A batter still at the crease simply equips themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is 'not out' is still in.
explanation.definitionFit: Indue, a variant of endue, means to endow or supply with something.

clue.text: Feeling the effects of fever and rash

explanation.surface: A patient feverish and covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a feverish head; figuratively impetuous and quick-tempered.

clue.text: Town guides, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to guide is to lead, so guides is leads

explanation.surface: Tour guides of a town, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major urban centre in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: A story or article about being in a foreign city

indicators.note: being in says the article and about pieces sit within the city name

parts.note: Rome is a city abroad from a British view
an is the indefinite article
c is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A news report about living in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link, and C for circa is a standard abbreviation; 'being in' sets AN and C within ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a tale, often of adventure or love.

clue.text: Mean with a girl

parts.note: the mean or average is the norm

explanation.surface: Someone is unkind to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female given name, so a girl may be called this.

clue.text: No place for the rider to change!

definitions.text: No place for the rider to change!

parts.words: No place for the rider to change!
parts.note: the proverb says you should not change horses in the middle of a river crossing, so the rider must not switch mounts at that spot

explanation.surface: A warning to a horseman not to swap mounts at the wrong moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'don't change horses in midstream' advises against switching plans halfway through a task.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names the middle of a river crossing as the point where changing mounts is unwise.

clue.text: An element most freely occurring in the sea

indicators.note: occurring in tells us the jumbled letters sit within the word for the sea

parts.note: brine is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so the word most is rearranged

explanation.surface: Some chemical element is found in great abundance in seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' looks like a quantity word but is the anagram fodder; 'freely' gives MSTO and 'occurring in' sets it within BRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is an old name for sulphur, a chemical element.

clue.text: A German, being very big hearted, turns red

indicators.note: big hearted means having the big piece at its heart, so it goes in the middle of the German word

parts.note: ein is German for a, so a German gives EIN
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning very big

explanation.surface: A generous German blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big hearted' suggests generosity; 'hearted' sets OS within EIN. 'turns' is a link, and eosin is a red dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red dye used to stain specimens in microscopy.

clue.text: The writer had a point about hard work

parts.note: E (east) is one of the compass points

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for hard work is read backwards

parts.note: toil is hard work

explanation.surface: An author made a fair argument concerning labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a point' sounds like making a fair argument; 'about' reverses TOIL to give LIOT after E.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T S Eliot are both famous authors.

clue.text: Such work could well be habit-forming

definitions.text: Such work could well be habit-forming

parts.words: Such work could well be habit-forming
parts.note: a habit is also a garment, so the work meant is making clothes, not forming an addiction

explanation.surface: Some jobs become addictive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's work forms garments, and a habit is a garment such as a monk's robe.

clue.text: Present one made time to exchange

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: exchange means swapping places, so the letters of made and time are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gift that someone created to swap with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but is the adjective meaning current; 'to exchange' rearranges MADE TIME to MMEDIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate, like present, describes something happening now, with no delay.

clue.text: Haven't got a game? That's unparalleled!

definitions.meaning: without any contest to play in

explanation.surface: Someone with no fixture this week declares the situation unique.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally without a contest; figuratively having no equal or rival.

clue.text: Agenda with VAT alternative takes precedence

indicators.note: alternative means another form, so the letters of agenda and vat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meeting plan prioritises a choice of tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges AGENDA VAT; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have advantage or precedence is to hold the superior position.

clue.text: "Never glad _____ morning again!" (Browning)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Robert Browning's poem The Lost Leader; the solver supplies the missing adjective in the line

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse lamenting a lost hope, with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank between 'glad' and 'morning'; the line from Browning's 'The Lost Leader' is completed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning's line describes a morning that is glad and sure of itself, the missing assured adjective.

clue.text: Small change made by the police

explanation.surface: The police take a tiny sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are both low-value coins and slang for police officers.

clue.text: Note on an old port

parts.note: D is a note in the musical scale
on top of something is over it

explanation.surface: A remark written about a historic harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is an ancient harbour town in Kent, one of the Cinque Ports on the English Channel.

clue.text: To tackle the problem yet again needs determination

definitions.text: To tackle the problem yet again
definitions.meaning: to work out the problem once more

explanation.surface: Trying the puzzle once more takes grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally solving once more; also firm intention or willpower.

clue.text: It's played in Ethiopia -nowhere else

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the run of letters across Ethiopia and nowhere

explanation.surface: A game or instrument found only in one African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'else' is a link word completing the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a musical instrument, which is played.

clue.text: A plea that's out of place

definitions.text: A plea that's out of place

parts.words: A plea that's out of place
parts.note: the plea is that the accused was elsewhere, out of the place of the crime, not that it is an improper plea

explanation.surface: An inappropriate appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence claiming the accused was elsewhere at the time.

clue.text: A woman in depression's all for friends

indicators.note: in says the woman piece goes inside the word for depressions

parts.note: a dent is a small depression, and the plural gives dents
her stands for a woman, as in the pronoun

explanation.surface: A depressed woman is wholly devoted to her companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all for' is a link: supporters are all for their cause. 'in' sets HER within DENTS, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are supporters or followers of a cause, much as friends back one another.

clue.text: Awestruck at a love-feast?

explanation.surface: Someone stunned at a romantic banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping in wonder; also the Greek word for the early Christians' communal fellowship meal.

clue.text: Stick with trendy sculptor

parts.note: a rod is a stick
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Keep to a fashionable artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was a French artist famous for The Thinker.

clue.text: Get rid of waste in America

definitions.meaning: to get rid of something is to remove or expel it
in American slang to waste someone is to kill them

explanation.surface: Disposing of rubbish in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Both remove something entirely: discarding it, or, in US slang, killing a person.

clue.text: Speak at length and inspire the Left

parts.note: to inspire is to breathe in, to draw breath
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A politician talks for ages to motivate the left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to talk slowly with stretched-out vowels.

clue.text: Hair-do for the stony?

definitions.meaning: a short tapered haircut fashionable in the 1920s
a beach of pebbles, a stony shore

explanation.surface: Asking which hairstyle suits a hard-hearted person.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle names both a cropped bob haircut and a pebbly beach.

clue.text: Faithful as serving men

parts.note: as can mean since, in the sense of because
RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the British army

explanation.surface: Loyal like servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving men' looks like servants; it is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person is genuine and true, as a faithful one is.
